newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HAMBURG SACK TRAINER MAGATH FOR SECOND TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAMBURG SACK TRAINER MAGATH FOR SECOND TIME.

text.p: Struggling German first division side Hamburg have sacked their controversial trainer Felix Magath -- the second time the club and their former midfield star have parted company in acrimony.
"I've worked my socks off here, that's well known," Magath said on Monday. "Obviously I'm an awkward person to deal with. And if you're awkward, you have enemies."

Magath, who scored Hamburg's winning goal in the 1983 European Cup final and played for Germany in the 1986 World Cup final, returned as trainer in October 1995 after another former Hamburg and Germany hero, Uwe Seeler, took over as club chairman.
Magath promptly led Hamburg out of the relegation zone and into a UEFA Cup berth. He extended his initial contract until 1999 and was given more extensive powers than any predecessor.
But Hamburg's league form this season has been poor and the players have been increasingly unsettled.
A dismal 4-0 home defeat to Cologne on Saturday left them in 15th place, one above the relegation zone.
It also became clear that the players were no longer behind Magath, leaving Seeler with little choice but to act.
"The chemistry you need wasn't there any more," Seeler said. "I couldn't see any prospect of improvement in the future."

The often unapproachable Magath had alienated a number of players with his emphasis on physical fitness and his ruthlessly disciplinarian approach, throwing out those such as midfielder Markus Schupp who dared to challenge him.
"I'm all in favour of hard work," Seeler said. "But even hard work ought to be fun."

Similar problems led to Magath's dismissal as team business manager in 1988 -- a job he held for two years after ending his playing career -- when he was widely blamed for the acrimonious departure of popular but outspoken goalkeeper Uli Stein.
Hamburg said Rolf Schehr, the trainer of the club's amateur side, would act as caretaker coach until the end of the season.
